evidence.why: int(u32), bits 3..7, no side effects.
GameModeState.id selects Classic entry and encounter setup.
Decoded state id copied into intro data.
Local round selects opponent table and flows to match setup.

reason: Exact pure bit extraction and independently read canonical mode callers establish progression-block semantics. RoundIndex remains a plausible descriptive hypothesis, not recovered spelling; eight-ID grouping means aligned blocks and repeats modulo 256.

evidence.why: All three transformations and exact color state transitions.
Accessor returns ncolors, or zero for out-of-range kind.
Caller supplies player kind/color and opponent arrays.

reason: Canonical signatures and loops prove bounded in-place costume repair, unresolved sentinel and assertion behavior; canonical accessor and Classic caller independently establish costume count and player/enemy mapping. These are targeted repairs, including preexisting active 0xFF entries, not universal duplicate removal.
